description: A unique identifier assigned to each product to facilitate tracking and identification within the company's inventory system. The code typically consists of alphanumeric characters.

A unique identifier assigned to a group of transactions processed as a single batch. This identifier is used to track and manage bulk operations, ensuring accurate reporting and reconciliation of grouped transactions.
The UNIX timestamp representing the exact moment a financial period ends, used to delineate the cutoff point for financial reporting or data aggregation.
Specifies the method through which a payment was made. This can include various forms such as electronic transfers, cash payments, credit card payments, etc.

Specifies the sub-category of the payment transaction, providing additional context beyond the primary payment type. This field is particularly useful for distinguishing between various kinds of transactions that fall under the same main category, such as differentiating between types of external payments.
The UNIX timestamp representing the date and time when the record was created. This value is measured in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1 1970 00:00:00 GMT).
A unique identifier representing a specific lifecycle of a financial product or service. This ID tracks the entire lifecycle, from inception through to termination, of the product or service.
Indicates the current status of a payment transaction, reflecting whether it has been successfully completed, is pending, or has failed.

related_business_terms.definition: The payment transaction has been successfully processed.
The payment transaction has been initiated but is not yet completed, often awaiting further action or confirmation.
The payment transaction could not be processed due to an error or rejection.

description: The Unix timestamp representing the specific time at which the execution of a financial transaction was requested by the user. This timestamp is measured in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970).

The Unix timestamp representing the exact date and time when the sender initiated the transaction. This value is expressed as the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), Thursday, 1 January 1970, not counting leap seconds.
Indicates whether a payment is set to occur at regular intervals. A TRUE value means the payment is recurring, while a FALSE value indicates a one-time payment.
This field represents the amount of money that the sender has transferred in a particular transaction. It is recorded in the transaction's currency and may include any applicable transaction fees.

This field represents the total number of payments scheduled for a financial transaction or obligation, such as a loan, lease, or any form of installment payment plan. It indicates the count of payments a borrower is obligated to make to fulfill the terms of the agreement.
The currency code representing the currency in which the transaction was initiated by the sender. This code follows the ISO 4217 currency code standard.
This field represents the bank account number from which the transaction is initiated. It is unique to the account holder and is used to identify the sender's account in financial transactions.
The name of the bank from which the funds are sent. This field identifies the financial institution initiating the transaction.

This field contains notes or descriptions provided by the sender related to the purpose or details of the transaction. It is used to give context or additional information about the transaction to the recipient.
This field represents the city in which the sender's bank is located. It is used to identify the geographical location of the bank involved in the financial transaction.
The postal code associated with the bank from which the funds are sent. This code helps in identifying the geographic location of the bank involved in the transaction.

The physical address of the bank from which the funds are being sent. This includes details such as street name, number, city, and sometimes the postal code, depending on the country. It is crucial for legal and verification purposes during the transaction process.
The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code representing the country of the bank initiating the transaction.
The name of the bank where the funds are being sent to in a financial transaction. This field captures the full legal name of the receiving financial institution.

The physical address of the bank where the receiver's account is held, including street name, number, city, and postal code. This information is crucial for identifying the specific branch for transactions, especially in international wire transfers.

The city in which the receiver's bank is located. This information is crucial for processing domestic and international financial transactions, ensuring that funds are directed to the correct local or regional banking institution.

This field represents the Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the bank where the receiver's account is held. The BIC is an international code that uniquely identifies financial and non-financial institutions.

This field represents the ISO country code of the bank where the recipient's account is held. It is used to identify the country in which the receiver's bank is located, facilitating international banking transactions.

The total amount of money received in a transaction, expressed in the transaction's currency. This value represents the net amount credited to the receiver's account, excluding any fees or adjustments.
The postal code associated with the physical location of the receiver's bank. This code is used to facilitate mail delivery and other services in the region where the bank is located.
This field represents the bank account number of the receiver involved in a transaction. It is a unique identifier used to route funds to the correct account during a financial transaction.
The city in which the receiver of a transaction or shipment is located.

Indicates the type of device used to access the service or perform the transaction. This can include various categories such as mobile phones, tablets, desktop computers, and other electronic devices capable of accessing the internet or running applications.

This field represents the longitudinal geographic coordinate where a device is located. Longitude values are measured in degrees, where negative values correspond to locations west of the Prime Meridian, and positive values correspond to locations east of the Prime Meridian.
The currency in which the transaction amount is processed for the receiver. This field specifies the type of currency used in a financial transaction from the perspective of the recipient.
This field represents the standardized two-letter country code of the country where the funds or services are being received. It adheres to the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.

The unique numerical label assigned to each device participating in a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication. This address serves both for identification and location addressing.

The geographical latitude coordinate where the device is located, expressed in decimal degrees. Positive values represent latitudes north of the equator, while negative values represent latitudes south of the equator.
A unique identifier assigned to events by external systems or partners. This identifier is used to reference the event across different platforms or databases outside the organization.

Specifies the type of financial event recorded in the transaction. This field categorizes the transaction by the nature of the financial activity it represents, such as payments, refunds, adjustments, etc.
Specifies the category of information being recorded, allowing users to distinguish between different types of data entries based on predefined categories.

The date on which a dispute was officially registered or initiated, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. This field is crucial for tracking the lifecycle of disputes and managing resolution timelines.

Describes the reason provided by a customer or a merchant for disputing a transaction. This field can include reasons such as fraudulent charges, services not provided, or incorrect transaction amount.

The date on which a financial dispute was resolved or closed, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the dispute has not been resolved or the end date is not available.

This field contains notes or comments related to disputes over transactions, charges, or other financial disagreements. It may include details on the nature of the dispute, actions taken, and the current status. This field can be particularly useful for financial analysts, customer service representatives, and compliance officers who are tracking the resolution of financial disputes.
Indicates whether a transaction dispute was refunded. This field can be null if the refund status is not applicable or unknown.

Represents the start date of an out-of-bounds (OOB) financial event or transaction, encoded as an integer. The value is typically formatted as YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the start date is not applicable or unknown.

This column contains textual notes or comments provided by the processing team or system regarding the feedback on disputes. These notes may include reasons for dispute decisions, additional information required, or any comments related to the dispute resolution process. The notes are intended for internal use to aid in the understanding and management of disputes.
Identifies the party who submitted the dispute. This could be the customer, merchant, or a third party acting on behalf of the customer.

related_business_terms.definition: A dispute occurs when a cardholder questions a transaction with their card issuer. The issuer creates a formal dispute, which immediately reverses the transaction.
A merchant is any type of business that sells goods or services.
An individual or business that purchases goods or services from a merchant.

An entity that is involved in some way in an interaction that is primarily between two other entities, such as a merchant and customer. In the context of disputes, this could refer to a legal representative or a payment processor.

description: Specifies the type of out-of-band communication used in transactions or security protocols. This field identifies the method by which additional verification or communication is conducted outside of the primary transaction channel.
The date on which a business officially ceased operations, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the business is still operational or the end date is unknown.

This field captures any textual notes or comments related to out-of-balance situations within financial transactions or accounts. It is used for documenting reasons, adjustments, or any relevant information that explains why a transaction or account balance does not match expected values. This can include discrepancies found during reconciliation processes, errors identified, or any adjustments made to rectify the balance.

This column captures any feedback notes provided through out-of-band (OOB) communication channels, such as emails, phone calls, or in-person meetings, regarding the performance, usability, or any other aspect of a product or service. These notes are valuable for qualitative analysis and for gaining insights that might not be captured through standard feedback mechanisms.
Categorizes user feedback into predefined labels for easier analysis and response. This field can be used to identify trends in user satisfaction and areas for improvement.
The name of the individual or entity initiating the transaction. This field captures the full name as a single string, including any middle names, initials, or suffixes.

Categorizes the nature of the feedback provided by a user or customer, indicating whether it is a complaint, suggestion, compliment, or inquiry. This field helps in analyzing customer feedback to improve products or services.

The email address of the individual or entity initiating the transaction or communication. This field captures the sender's email in a standardized format, facilitating contact tracing, authentication, and verification processes.

This field represents the phone number of the individual or entity initiating the transaction. It is stored as a string of digits without any formatting, such as dashes or parentheses. The phone number includes the country code but excludes any leading zeros or plus signs.

Specifies the type of out-of-band (OOB) response used in a transaction or authentication process. This field can indicate the method through which a secondary verification is performed, such as SMS, email, or a push notification. A null value suggests that no out-of-band response was required or recorded.
The ZIP code from which the item was sent. This is used to identify the postal area of the sender's address.
This field represents the date of birth of the individual or entity sending the transaction. The date is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.
This field represents the type of account from which funds are being sent. It identifies whether the account is a checking, savings, or other types of financial account.
The currency code representing the currency of the funds in the sender's account. This code follows the ISO 4217 currency code standard.
The Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the account sending the transaction. It is an international code that uniquely identifies financial and non-financial institutions.
A unique identifier assigned to entities receiving transactions or payments, ensuring accurate tracking and reporting of financial activities.

This field represents the current balance of the sender's account in a financial transaction. It is a floating-point number that reflects the amount of money available in the account after the transaction has been initiated but before it has been completed.

The full name of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or payment. This field captures the recipient's name as recorded in the transaction details, ensuring accurate identification for accounting and reporting purposes.

The phone number of the individual or entity receiving a transaction or communication. This number is expected to be in a standardized international format without spaces or special characters, starting with the country code.

The email address of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or communication. This field is used to identify the recipient in various financial operations, such as payments, notifications, and account updates.

The street address of the recipient or receiver in a transaction. This address is used for billing or shipping purposes and includes the house number, street name, and any applicable suite or apartment numbers.

The ZIP code associated with the address of the recipient in a transaction. This field captures the postal code where the receiver or beneficiary of a transaction is located, facilitating geographic analysis and validation of addresses.

Indicates the employment status of the sender at the time of the transaction. This field helps in understanding the sender's economic background and can be used for analytics related to financial behavior based on employment status.

related_business_terms.definition: Indicates the sender is currently employed and receives a regular income.
Indicates the sender is not currently employed and does not receive a regular income from employment.
Indicates the sender runs their own business or works on a freelance basis.
Indicates the sender has retired from active employment and may receive a pension or retirement income.
Indicates the sender is currently enrolled in a full-time or part-time educational program and may not have a regular income.

description: The date of birth of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or service. This field is used to verify identity and for age-related requirements.
This field represents the geographical region or area code of the receiver in a transaction. It is used to identify the location within a country where the receiver of a transaction is based.
A unique identifier assigned to each device used in financial transactions. This ID helps in tracking and managing devices across various platforms and services.

This field specifies the currency in which the receiver's account is denominated. It is used to identify the currency type for transactions, ensuring that currency conversion and reconciliation processes can be accurately performed.

Indicates the type of account that is receiving funds in a transaction. This field specifies the nature of the receiver's bank account, such as whether it is a checking, savings, or other types of financial accounts.

This field represents the type of channel through which a transaction or interaction was initiated or completed. It categorizes the medium or platform used, providing insights into customer preferences and behavior.
Unique identifier for the bank branch of the sender. This ID is used to specify the originating branch of a transaction or transfer.
A six-digit number that identifies the bank and branch where a bank account is held. Used primarily in the United Kingdom to route money transfers between banks.
A six-digit number that identifies the bank branch of the account holder used in the UK and Irish banking industry to route money transfers between banks.
Indicates the direction of a financial transaction, specifying whether funds are moving out of an account (OUTBOUND) or into an account.

A unique code that identifies the financial institution of the receiver in a transaction. It is used to direct funds to the correct bank during a transaction, ensuring the secure and efficient transfer of funds.
Specifies the method used for user authentication.
The UNIX timestamp indicating when the event occurred, measured in the number of seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1 1970 00:00:00 GMT).
Defines the type of channel through which a customer segment interacts or is targeted. This includes both digital and physical channels.
A unique identifier for a user's session, typically used to track user activity or engagement within an application or website over a specific period.
Specifies the type of alias used to identify the sender in a transaction. This field categorizes the method or format in which the sender is represented.

A two-letter country code representing the country associated with the device's IP address. This code is determined based on the geographical location of the IP address and follows the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.

This field represents the language setting of the user's device, typically denoting the primary language used for display and input. It follows the IETF BCP 47 language tag standard, combining ISO 639-1 language codes and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes.

This field contains custom messages or instructions intended for the receiver of the transaction. It is often used in payment processing to provide additional details or thanks related to the payment.
A unique identifier generated for each device based on its hardware and software configurations. This identifier is used to track devices for security and fraud detection purposes.
Indicates whether the instant transfer request passed the financial institution's review process. A TRUE value means the transfer was approved, while a FALSE implies it was rejected.

This field captures the name of the web browser used by the visitor or user to access the website or application. It helps in understanding the browser distribution among users for optimizing web performance and compatibility.
This field represents the ZIP code associated with the sender's account address. It is used to identify the geographical location of the sender for transaction processing and verification purposes.
Indicates the type of bank initiating the transaction. This field categorizes banks based on their primary function and services offered.
The name of the company or entity that is the recipient of a transaction, product, or service.
The geographical region associated with the device's IP address, typically represented as a two-letter country code.

A unique identifier for the set of rules applied within the Condor financial analysis system. These codes categorize various financial conditions, actions, or compliance checks that need to be performed on financial data.

This field captures the identifying details of the browser and operating system used by the device initiating a transaction or accessing the application. It is a string that can be parsed to understand the device type, operating system, browser version, and other device-specific features.
sample_values: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 14_4 like Mac OS X)

description: Indicates whether the feedback provided by a user is positive (TRUE) or negative (FALSE). This boolean value helps in understanding user satisfaction and areas of improvement.

This field represents the matched company name of the transaction receiver, as identified in the company's operations platform. It is used to ensure that transactions are correctly associated with the right corporate entities.
This field contains details about the scheduling of recurring payments, indicating the frequency at which these payments are expected to occur.
Specifies the method used by the sender to authenticate the transaction. This field can include various types of authentication methods such as biometric, PIN, or password verification.
A unique identifier for each office location within the organization, used to track and manage office-specific data, resources, and activities.

A unique code identifying the type of Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) processing applied to a payment transaction. This code helps in categorizing the transaction based on the level and type of authentication used, in compliance with regulatory requirements.
Indicates the ownership type of the account from which funds are being sent. This field helps in identifying whether the account is owned by an individual or a corporate entity.

Categorizes customers based on market segmentation criteria such as purchasing behavior, demographic profile, and engagement level. This classification helps in tailoring marketing strategies and product offerings to meet the specific needs of each segment.
Specifies the type of message or format used for a payment instruction. This can include different standards or formats depending on the payment system or network.
Specifies the type of transaction initiated by the sender. This field identifies the method or channel through which the transaction is executed.

related_business_terms.definition: Automated Clearing House. A network used for electronic payments and money transfers. ACH is a way to move money between banks without using paper checks, wire transfers, credit card networks, or cash.

description: A unique code assigned to a payment revision, indicating the type or reason for the revision. This code helps in tracking and managing payment adjustments or corrections.

Indicates the classification type of the bank receiving a transaction. This field categorizes banks based on their primary function, such as retail, commercial, or investment, to facilitate targeted analysis and processing.
The unique identifier assigned to banks where the receiver's account is held. This ID helps in identifying the specific bank in financial transactions.
The date on which the sender's phone number was last updated or changed in the system. The date is recorded in the format YYYY-MM-DD.

This field represents the alternative name or alias used by a Third-Party Payment (TPP) service provider. It is used for identification purposes in cases where the TPP is known by multiple names or has undergone rebranding.
Indicates the role of the third-party payment processor (TPP) in the transaction, specifying whether the TPP is acting as the payee (receiving payment) or the payer (making payment).
Represents the total count of payments made by an individual or entity within a specified time frame. This count includes all completed transactions that were processed as payments.

The unique identifier of the branch where the customer primarily conducts their banking activities. This ID is used to associate a customer with their main branch within the financial institution's network.

A unique identifier assigned to each recurring payment transaction to facilitate tracking and management. This reference is used to identify individual transactions in a series of automated payments, ensuring accurate record-keeping and reconciliation.

Indicates the classification of the customer based on the nature of the account holder. This field distinguishes between individual customers and other types of customers, such as corporate entities, depending on the financial institution's categorization criteria.
A unique identifier assigned to each phone session, used to track and manage calls within the system.
A unique identifier assigned by the sender to a transaction for tracking and reference purposes. This reference helps in identifying transactions in statements and reports.

This field contains detailed information about the payment, including the purpose and any additional details necessary for the recipient to match the payment with an invoice or service. It is typically used in financial transactions to provide clarity on what the payment is for, especially in business-to-business transactions.
A unique code representing the category of the transaction initiated by the sender. This code helps in classifying the transaction for reporting and analytics purposes.

A globally unique identifier (GUID) representing an individual user within the system. This identifier is used to uniquely identify users across the platform, ensuring data integrity and consistency in user-related transactions and analytics.
Indicates the origin of the transaction or message sender, specifying the platform or medium used.
A unique identifier associated with a payment or transaction, facilitating tracking and reconciliation of payments across financial systems.

A descriptive text provided by the sender detailing the purpose or nature of the transaction. This narrative helps in identifying the reason for the payment and can be used for reconciliation, reporting, and compliance purposes.
Indicates the current operational status of the bank initiating the transaction. This status can affect the ability to process transactions.

The official name of the corporation initiating the transaction. This field captures the full legal name as registered in the corporation's founding documents or as legally recognized by the jurisdiction in which the corporation operates.
This field represents the method through which a customer was onboarded onto the platform or service. It indicates whether the onboarding process was completed digitally or through other means.

related_business_terms.definition: The process of integrating a new customer using digital tools and platforms, without the need for physical interaction.
The process of integrating a new customer through face-to-face interactions, typically in an office or branch location.
The process of integrating a new customer through telephonic conversations, guiding them through the necessary steps over a call.
The process of integrating a new customer by sending them necessary information and steps through email.

description: The name of the company initiating the transaction. This field captures the full legal name of the entity that is sending the transaction, providing clarity on the transaction origin for auditing and tracking purposes.

The date on which the email address associated with the receiver's account was last changed. This field is used to track updates to a receiver's contact information for communication or security purposes.

This field represents the external account number of the sender. It is used to uniquely identify the sender's account in transactions that involve external financial institutions or systems. The account number is typically assigned and recognized outside of the organization's internal systems.
Indicates the current operational status of the bank intended to receive a transaction or payment. This status helps in determining if the bank is capable of processing incoming transactions.

The date on which the email address of the sender was last updated or changed. This field is critical for tracking the history of sender email updates and ensuring contact information is current. The value is stored in a YYYY-MM-DD format.

This field contains detailed information about the recipient of a transaction, including but not limited to the name, account number, and other identifying details. It is crucial for ensuring transactions are directed to the correct party.
The name of the Third Party Provider involved in the financial transaction or service.

Categorizes the type of merchant receiving the transaction, based on the standard merchant classification codes. This field helps in identifying the sector or industry to which the merchant belongs, providing insights into spending patterns and sector-based transaction analysis.
The date on which the customer's primary work phone number was last updated or changed in the system. The date is recorded in the YYYY-MM-DD format.

Unique identifier code for the Store and Forward (SAF) payment transaction. This code is used to track and manage payments that are initially stored due to network issues or processing delays and are forwarded for processing at a later time.

The date on which the customer's second work phone number was last updated or changed in the system. This field tracks any modifications to a secondary work contact number to maintain up-to-date contact information.

The date on which the customer's secondary home phone number was last updated or changed in the system. This field tracks changes to ensure contact information is current and can be used for verification purposes or customer service follow-ups.

A unique identifier used to track the lifecycle of a financial product or service in alternative systems or databases. It is used for cross-referencing and integrating data across different platforms or systems.
Represents the total number of financial accounts (e.g., checking, savings, loans, etc.) a customer holds with the financial institution.

The date on which the customer's primary home phone number was last updated or changed. This field captures any updates to the customer's primary contact number, ensuring accurate and up-to-date contact information is maintained.

Indicates the classification of the customer's account based on predefined criteria such as account features, benefits, and eligibility requirements. This classification helps in providing tailored financial services and products.

The date on which the customer's primary mobile phone number was last updated or changed in the system. This field helps in tracking the most recent contact information update for a customer to ensure all communications are sent to the correct mobile number.

The date on which the customer's secondary mobile phone number was last updated or changed in the system. This field captures any modifications made to the secondary mobile phone number, including updates to the number itself or changes in the phone number's details.

Describes the purpose or reason behind the transaction initiated by the sender. This field provides insights into the nature of the transaction, helping in categorizing and understanding the transaction flow.
This field represents the original currency in which the transaction was initiated by the sender, before any currency conversion.
The original amount of money that the sender intended to transfer before any fees or currency conversion. This value represents the gross amount sent by the initiator of the transaction.

This field represents the type of product or service selected by the sender for executing the transaction. It indicates the level or category of service chosen, which may affect the transaction speed, cost, and other conditions.

Specifies the type of product or service involved in the transaction received. This field categorizes the transaction based on the product type, facilitating the identification and analysis of the transaction nature.

Indicates the result of the Confirmation of Payee (CoP) check for a transaction initiated by the sender. This check is performed to ensure the name of the account holder matches the name provided by the sender for the transaction.
The amount of money sent by the sender in a transaction, expressed in United States Dollars (USD). This value represents the monetary amount before any transaction fees or adjustments.
Indicates the origin of the payment initiation message. This field identifies the platform or method through which the payment was initiated.
A unique identifier assigned to third-party processors involved in transaction processing. This ID is used to track and manage transactions processed by external entities.

This field represents the timezone setting of the user's browser, indicating the geographical or political region based on which the local time is determined. It is crucial for ensuring that timestamps and time-related data are accurately displayed to users according to their local time.

This field represents the primary channel through which a customer's portfolio is managed or accessed. It indicates whether the portfolio interactions are predominantly digital, in-person, via telephone, or through other channels.

Indicates the operating system platform of the device used by the customer. This field helps in understanding the distribution of users across different operating systems, aiding in targeted marketing and app development strategies.
Classifies customers based on the type of portfolio they hold with the financial institution, indicating the level of service and products available to them.
This field represents the geographical region of the customer's portfolio, categorizing where the majority of the customer's investments or accounts are held or managed.
The timestamp representing the date and time at which data was recorded or an event occurred on the device, expressed as the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC).
This field represents the type of financial product held by the customer within their portfolio. It includes various banking and investment products offered by the financial institution.
This field represents the country associated with the customer's investment portfolio. It indicates the country where the portfolio is primarily held or managed.

Categorizes customers based on the classification criteria defined by the financial institution, which often includes factors such as investment size, risk tolerance, and investment objectives. This classification helps in providing tailored financial advice and products.
The UNIX timestamp indicating when the event was received by the system. This value represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (midnight on January 1, 1970, UTC).

A unique identifier assigned to each transaction document generated by the device. This identifier is used to track and retrieve transaction documents for auditing, troubleshooting, and reporting purposes.

This field represents the old or previous value associated with a customer attribute before an update or change was made. It is used to track changes in customer-related data over time, enabling historical comparisons and data integrity checks.

Categorizes the computing power of the device's CPU into predefined classes based on processing capabilities. This classification helps in understanding the device's performance level and can be used to tailor application behavior or content delivery accordingly.

This field represents the new value assigned to a customer attribute following a change. It captures the updated information post any modification action, such as a change in customer name, address, or contact details.

A unique identifier assigned to each consent record, facilitating the tracking and management of user consents across systems. This identifier is crucial for compliance with data protection and privacy regulations, ensuring that user preferences are accurately recorded and adhered to.
Indicates the type of device used for banking activities, categorizing the banking interaction based on the technological medium.

Identifies the method or technology used for generating a device fingerprint. This fingerprint is unique to each device based on its hardware and software configurations, and is used for tracking and identifying devices across sessions for security, fraud detection, and analytics purposes.
The domain name of the website associated with the entity. This field contains the base URL without any subdomains, paths, or protocols.

The IPv6 address assigned to a device connected to the internet. IPv6 addresses are alphanumeric, divided into eight groups, and use a colon to separate each group. This format allows for a vast number of unique IP addresses.
A unique identifier assigned to users within a specific channel or platform, used to track user interactions and activities.
A unique alphanumeric code assigned to a transaction initiated by the sender. This code is used to identify and track the transaction throughout the payment processing system.

A numerical score representing the assessed risk level of an entity, calculated through a proprietary algorithm that evaluates various risk factors. The score is presented as a string for compatibility with systems requiring textual data. It is used to gauge the potential risk an entity poses, facilitating risk management and decision-making processes.
Indicates the origin of the data entry, specifying the platform or method through which the data was collected or entered.

The date on which the transaction initiated by the sender is set to expire. This field indicates the last day the transaction can be processed or needs to be completed by. The format follows the ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DD).
A unique identifier assigned to each customer for identification and record-keeping purposes.

Indicates the security level of camera authorization required or assigned within a security system. This level determines the access control and surveillance capabilities based on predefined security protocols.

Describes the reason for the classification of the device platform type, providing insights into how the platform was determined, such as through detection of mobile characteristics or user-agent analysis.
Specifies the type of request initiated in a financial transaction or operation. It defines the nature of the transaction being requested by the user or system.

Indicates the signing status of a transaction initiated by the sender. This status determines if the transaction has been digitally signed by the sender, which is a crucial step for authentication and non-repudiation of transactions.
Specifies the method used for user authentication within the system, indicating the security protocol for accessing accounts.
A unique identifier representing the collection of investments held by a customer. This identifier is used to track and manage the customer's investments across different asset classes.
A unique identifier assigned to each customer on a global scale, ensuring consistency and uniqueness across all regions and systems.

Indicates the classification of the account based on its purpose or the account holder's relationship with the financial institution. This field categorizes accounts into different types such as personal, business, or other specific classifications that determine the nature of the account.

related_business_terms.definition: A bank account owned by an individual that is used for personal banking transactions, excluding business or commercial activities.

The process of categorizing bank accounts based on specific criteria such as the account holder's type (individual or business), the purpose of the account (savings, checking, loan, etc.), or other distinguishing features.

description: The date when the customer's phone number was last updated in the system. This field tracks any changes made to a customer's phone number, ensuring accurate and up-to-date contact information is maintained. The date is recorded in the format YYYY-MM-DD.

The date on which the customer's email address was last updated. This field captures any changes made to the customer's email, providing a historical record of updates for contact information verification and audit purposes.
The date on which the customer's address was last updated in the system. This field is recorded in the format YYYY-MM-DD to ensure consistency and ease of sorting and filtering.
A unique identifier assigned to customers by external systems or partners. This ID is used to reference customers across different platforms or databases without exposing internal IDs.
Indicates if the sender of the transaction is the sole initiator. This field is used to identify transactions initiated by a single entity without joint parties.
The currency in which a customer's account is denominated. This indicates the currency type used for all transactions within the customer's account.

A unique identifier assigned to a customer's account for external reference purposes. This alphanumeric string is used to link the account across different systems or databases without revealing sensitive internal account details.

A unique identifier assigned to each customer's account, used for identifying and managing customer information across financial systems. It is critical for transaction processing, account management, and customer service.
The ZIP code associated with the customer's account address. This field is used for mailing purposes and may also be used in geographic analysis and customer segmentation.
The name of the platform or medium through which a customer interacts with services or products. This could include digital platforms, physical locations, or other mediums.
A unique identifier assigned to each staff member within the organization. It is used for tracking and managing employee records, payroll, and access to systems.
The country associated with the customer's account, represented by a two-letter country code based on the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.

This field specifies the currency denomination for the daily transaction limit applicable to a particular channel. It indicates the type of currency in which the daily limits are calculated and enforced.
A unique identifier assigned to each workstation within the organization. It is used to track and manage assets, ensuring each workstation's configurations and assets are accurately recorded.
A unique identifier assigned to a device token used for secure transactions or authentication purposes.

The unique media access control (MAC) address assigned to a network interface controller (NIC) for use as a network address in communications within a network segment. This address is used for identification and location tracking.
Specifies the type of identifier used for user identification. This can include various forms of identifiers, but this column specifically denotes the format or category of the identifier.

related_business_terms.User Identification: The process or the method used to recognize or verify the identity of a user within a system.
related_business_terms.Authentication: The process of verifying the identity of a user when they log into a system.
related_business_terms.Data Privacy: Refers to the handling, processing, and storage of personal identification information in compliance with applicable privacy laws and regulations.

description: Indicates the presence of detailed transaction information from the sender's perspective. This field can help in identifying transactions that include additional descriptive information about the transaction, aiding in more granular analysis and reporting.
Unique identifier for the entity responsible for the payment transaction. This could represent a business, individual, or any other legal entity involved in the payment process.
Categorizes the nature of the transaction initiated by the sender, indicating the purpose or type of transaction being conducted.

related_business_terms.definition: A classification that provides insights into the purpose of a financial transaction, such as personal, business, or others.
The party that initiates a transaction, transferring funds or value from one account or individual to another.

description: A unique identifier assigned by the sender to each transaction for tracking and reference purposes. This alphanumeric string facilitates the matching and reconciliation of transactions between the sender and the recipient.
Indicates the current status of a transaction initiated by the sender. This status provides insights into the transaction's lifecycle and helps in tracking its progress.

Describes the reason behind the current status of a transaction initiated by the sender. This field provides insights into the transaction's outcome or any errors that might have occurred during the processing phase.

An alternative reference number assigned by the sender to uniquely identify a transaction. This field is used for tracking and reconciliation purposes, especially in cases where the primary reference number is not available or applicable.

This field captures alternative reasons provided by customers for any changes made to their account or service preferences. It includes detailed explanations beyond standard reason codes, offering insights into customer behavior and decision-making processes.
Indicates the method chosen by the customer to receive notifications about changes in the delivery of their order, such as updates or delays.

The date on which the transaction initiated by the sender is scheduled to take effect. This field represents the planned date for the transaction to be applied or recognized in the system or ledger. It is crucial for ensuring that transactions are processed in a timely manner and helps in the reconciliation and tracking of financial activities.
Represents the amount of money associated with a user's transaction or account balance, formatted as a string to accommodate various currency symbols and decimal separators.
This field represents the unique number associated with a customer's credit or debit card. It is used to identify the card in transactions.

A unique identifier assigned to users for the purpose of tracking their interactions or status within a system. This alphanumeric code helps in differentiating users and analyzing their behavior or preferences.
A unique identifier or string associated with a user, often representing usernames, user IDs, or any form of text-based user identification.
A unique identifier assigned to each entity within the system. This identifier is used to uniquely distinguish one entity from another and is critical for data tracking, referencing, and integrity.
A unique identifier for a session where a user's identity is being verified. This ID is used to track and manage individual identity verification processes throughout the system.
A unique identifier for specific events or transactions within a financial system. It categorizes the nature and type of the event being recorded.

Defines the type of entity involved in the transaction or account. It categorizes the entity into various predefined types such as customer, vendor, partner, etc., to facilitate differentiated processing and reporting.
The city identified from the device's IP address, indicating the geographical location where the device is being used.
The country code associated with the geographic location of the device, determined by the device's IP address. This code is represented in a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format.

The Internet Service Provider (ISP) associated with the device's IP address, derived from geolocation services. This field identifies the ISP that provides internet service to the device based on its current IP address.
Indicates whether the GPS functionality is enabled on the device. This field is crucial for applications that require location data to provide services or analytics.

The URL of the webpage that a user was on before reaching the current page, indicating where the traffic originated from. This information is crucial for analyzing the sources of website traffic and understanding user navigation behavior.

This field represents the geographic longitude coordinate of a device. Longitude values are measured in degrees, where negative values indicate west of the Prime Meridian and positive values indicate east. This data is crucial for geo-location services, mapping, and location-based analytics.

Represents the IANA Time Zone database name corresponding to the geographic location of the device. This information is crucial for localizing the timestamps of device activities based on its geographical location.

This field represents the geographic latitude coordinate where the device is located. Latitude values are expressed as decimal degrees, where positive values indicate latitudes north of the equator, and negative values indicate latitudes south of the equator.

This field represents the Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID) of the Wi-Fi network a device is currently connected to. The BSSID is a unique identifier associated with the access point (AP) within a Wi-Fi network, typically represented as a MAC address.

Indicates whether an entity (individual or organization) has been checked against global financial sanction lists. A TRUE value means the entity is found on a sanction list, whereas FALSE means the entity is not found on any such list.
Indicates whether the device has data collection and reporting enabled. A TRUE value means data collection is active, allowing for monitoring and analysis of device performance and usage.
Indicates whether the Bluetooth feature is enabled on a device. This can be used to determine if a device is capable of connecting to other devices or systems via Bluetooth.

Indicates whether any WiFi network is within the range of the device's WiFi sensor. This is typically used to determine if the device can potentially connect to a WiFi network without specifying the availability or strength of the network.

A list of identifiers for Bluetooth devices that are currently connected to the device. This data is typically collected from devices that have Bluetooth capabilities and are able to connect to other Bluetooth-enabled devices. The identifiers are unique to each Bluetooth device and can be used to track which devices were connected at a specific point in time.

Represents the Mobile Country Code (MCC) associated with the device's mobile network. MCC is a unique identifier used in combination with a Mobile Network Code (MNC) to identify mobile phone networks and operators in different countries.

A comma-separated list of identifiers for Bluetooth devices that were detected within range of the scanning device. This list is dynamically generated based on the Bluetooth devices that are present and discoverable in the vicinity of the scanning device at the time of the scan.

The International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) associated with the user's mobile device. It is a unique identifier for the user of a cellular network and is stored as a 64-bit field and can be up to 15 digits long. It is used for securing mobile networks and identifying users uniquely on the network.

Indicates whether the device has native codehooks enabled, allowing for more advanced integration and functionality within the device's operating system. This field can be particularly relevant in environments where enhanced security or custom features are implemented at a low level.
Indicates whether a debugger is attached to the device, which may suggest development or testing activity, or potential security risks if found in production environments.

Indicates whether the device is using a keyboard that is not trusted or certified. A value of TRUE means the device is using an untrusted keyboard, while FALSE means the device is using a trusted keyboard.
Indicates whether the JavaScript executed on the device during a transaction was malformed, potentially signifying an attempt to tamper with or bypass client-side validation or security measures.

Indicates whether a screen reader, which is not trusted, is active on the device. This can be used as a security measure to detect potential fraudulent access attempts or to ensure compatibility with accessibility tools.

Indicates whether the device is using any hooking frameworks, which can intercept and potentially alter the execution flow of software on the device. This is commonly used in testing environments or by malicious software to monitor or modify other applications' behavior.

Indicates whether the application on the device has been repackaged, which may suggest tampering or modification from its original version. A value of TRUE means the application has been altered, while FALSE implies the application remains in its original, unmodified state.

This field represents the raw, unprocessed Joule per Square Centimeter (J/SC) measurement data collected from a device. It captures the energy measurement in terms of Joules per square centimeter, which is crucial for understanding the energy efficiency or output of the device in question. This raw data is essential for further analysis and calibration processes.

A numerical score representing the assessed risk level of a device, based on various factors such as device history, transaction patterns, and known security vulnerabilities. The score ranges from 0 to 100, where a higher score indicates a higher risk.
Indicates whether the user's device is a desktop computer. A TRUE value means the device is a desktop, while FALSE indicates it is not.
A unique identifier generated from the characteristics of a user's device, such as hardware configuration, browser attributes, and IP address, used for tracking and fraud prevention purposes.

Indicates whether the device used is a game console. This can help in understanding the type of devices that are accessing the service, allowing for better targeting and optimization of content and services for gaming platforms.
Indicates whether the device has been rooted or jailbroken, providing unauthorized access to the device's software. A value of TRUE means the device is rooted, while FALSE indicates it is not.

This field represents the timezone setting of the device at the time of the transaction or event. It is stored in the IANA Time Zone Database format, which provides a reliable way to identify the world's timezones.

The city associated with the IP address of the device. This information is typically derived from geolocation services that map IP addresses to geographical locations, providing insights into where the device accessing the service is located.
Indicates the current status of a financial event, such as a transaction or an operational activity, within the system. It helps in tracking the progress and completion of the event.

Represents the geographic longitude coordinate estimated from the device's IP address. This value is used to identify the approximate physical location of the device accessing the service or application.

Represents the latitude coordinate associated with the device's IP address. This value is derived from geo-location services that map IP addresses to geographical locations. Latitude values range from -90.0 to 90.0, where positive values indicate latitudes north of the Equator, and negative values indicate latitudes south of the Equator.
A two-letter code representing the country of the customer, following the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.
The postal code associated with a customer's billing address. This information is used for shipping, billing, and regional analysis purposes.

Categorizes customers based on their attributes, behavior, or value to the organization. This classification helps in tailoring marketing strategies, product development, and services to meet the specific needs of each segment.
The full name of the customer as recorded in the transaction or account. This field may include first name, middle name, last name, and any suffixes or titles.

related_business_terms.KYC: Know Your Customer - a standard in the finance industry that ensures investment advisors know detailed information about their clients' risk tolerance, investment knowledge, and financial position.
related_business_terms.Customer Identification Program: A requirement for financial institutions to verify the identity of individuals wishing to conduct financial transactions with them to prevent fraud and money laundering.

description: The full address of the customer, including street number, street name, city, state, and ZIP code.

Represents the date of birth of the customer, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD. This field is crucial for calculating the age of the customer for various financial products eligibility and compliance with age-related regulations.
A unique identifier assigned to each customer. It is used to track and manage customer information across various systems and databases.

A unique identifier assigned to each branch of a financial institution where a customer holds an account. This ID is used to distinguish between different branches within the same organization, facilitating location-specific data analysis and operational reporting.
The primary contact number provided by a customer, including the country code without any separators.
Indicates whether the device accessing the service is an emulator or a physical device. A value of TRUE means the device is an emulator, while FALSE implies a physical device.
A unique identifier for an account within the financial system. It is used to track and manage accounts across various operations and transactions.
Indicates whether JavaScript is enabled on the user's device. This can be critical for understanding if dynamic content or web applications can be properly utilized by the end user.
This field contains the email addresses of customers. It is used as a unique identifier for communication and identification purposes within the system.
Identifies the channel through which a transaction or interaction was initiated or completed.

Indicates whether the transaction initiated by the sender is directed towards a new beneficiary that has not been previously paid. A value of TRUE means this is the first transaction to the new beneficiary, while FALSE indicates the beneficiary has been paid before.
Indicates whether the device's Wi-Fi connection is active or not. A TRUE value means the Wi-Fi is connected and operational, while FALSE indicates that the device is not connected to a Wi-Fi network.

Indicates whether the transaction initiated by the sender is currently being held for review or processing. A TRUE value signifies that the transaction is on hold, while FALSE indicates that the transaction is not being held and is processing normally.

Represents the difference in hours and minutes from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for the device's local time zone. The format is signed, indicating the direction (ahead or behind UTC) and the offset in hours and minutes.

Indicates whether the payment was made from the account holder's own account. A TRUE value means the payment was made from the account holder's own account, while a FALSE value means the payment was made from a different account.

Indicates whether the use of a specific payment template is restricted. A value of TRUE means the template is restricted and cannot be used for transactions without specific permissions. A value of FALSE means the template is not restricted and can be freely used for transactions.
Indicates whether the payment method for a transaction is direct debit. A TRUE value means the payment was made using direct debit, while FALSE means another payment method was used.
Indicates the level of urgency or priority assigned by the sender to a message or transaction. This field helps in prioritizing processing and response actions based on the urgency level.

related_business_terms.Messaging Priority: The importance level assigned to a message to determine processing priority.
related_business_terms.Transaction Urgency: A classification used to prioritize transactions based on the sender's urgency level.

description: The local date and time when the sender initiated the transaction, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. This timestamp reflects the local time zone of the sender at the moment of transaction initiation.

Represents the average balance of the sender's account over a specified period, indicating the general state of the account's funds. This metric is crucial for assessing the financial health and stability of the account holder.

This field represents the maximum amount of money that can be transacted through a specific channel (e.g., ATM, online banking, mobile app) within a single day. It is used to set limits to ensure security and manage liquidity.
A unique identifier or code representing a specific set of transactions or financial data within a matrix format, used for analysis or reporting purposes.

The Unix timestamp representing the date and time when the receiver's account was created. This value is expressed as the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC).

The date on which the sender was registered in the system, represented as the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970). This field is crucial for understanding the tenure of the sender within the platform and can be used for analyzing user behavior over time.

This column contains unique identifiers or data related to biocatalysts used in various chemical processes. Biocatalysts are enzymes or microorganisms that accelerate chemical reactions. The data is represented as a string and can include codes, names, or any relevant information pertaining to the biocatalyst.

The UNIX timestamp representing the exact moment an event was validated by the server. This field captures the time at which the server confirmed the event's data integrity and authenticity, ensuring it meets all necessary validation criteria before processing. The timestamp is represented as the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).
A unique identifier assigned to each user within the system. It is used to track and manage user information across various databases and services.

The UNIX timestamp indicating the last time the event was updated. This value represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC) to the event's last update time.
The name of the bank where the receiver's account is held. This field identifies the financial institution responsible for the receipt of a transaction.

This field captures the latest updates or changes made to customer information, reflecting the most recent data entered into the system. It is a string representation of the new data points that have been added or modified for a customer's profile.

Specifies the sub-category of the payment type, providing further detail on the nature of the transaction. It helps in distinguishing between various forms of payment types under the same main category.

This field represents the operating system running on a user's device, including the version number. It is crucial for understanding the software environment in which mobile or desktop applications are operating, enabling targeted software updates and compatibility checks.

This field contains the previous or historical data related to a customer before an update or change was made. It is stored as a string and can include various types of information depending on the context, such as address, contact details, or account preferences.
A unique identifier assigned to electronic devices within the enterprise system, facilitating device management and tracking.
A unique identifier assigned to each device during its development phase, used for tracking and identification purposes in various systems.

This column lists the identifiers of the specific rules that were triggered during the transaction validation process. Each rule is designed to flag specific conditions or anomalies based on predefined criteria. The values are represented as strings, where each string corresponds to a unique rule identifier.

related_business_terms.Rule Identifier: A unique identifier assigned to a specific rule within the transaction validation system.
related_business_terms.Transaction Validation: The process of verifying transactions to ensure they comply with predefined rules and regulations.
related_business_terms.Anomaly Detection: The identification of items, events, or observations which do not conform to an expected pattern or other items in a dataset.

description: Represents the final decision made on a financial application or request, indicating whether it was approved or not. This decision is typically the result of an evaluation process that considers various financial and non-financial factors.

Indicates the type of transaction being recorded. This field categorizes each transaction by its nature, such as payments, refunds, transfers, etc., to facilitate easier tracking and reporting of financial activities.

related_business_terms.PAYMENT: A transaction where a sum of money is transferred from one party to another, typically as compensation for goods or services.
related_business_terms.REFUND: A transaction where money previously paid is returned to the payer, often due to overpayment or dissatisfaction with goods or services.
related_business_terms.TRANSFER: A transaction where money is moved from one account to another without any exchange of goods or services.

description: Categorizes the level of risk associated with an investment's outcome, based on various financial models and historical data analysis. It is used to guide investors in understanding potential risk exposure.

A numerical score representing the likelihood of a decision being declined, based on the outcome of a predictive model. The score ranges from 0 to 1, where a higher score indicates a greater likelihood of the decision being declined.
A numerical score representing the likelihood of an outcome being approved, based on a predictive model. Scores range from 0 to 1, where a higher score indicates a higher probability of approval.

A numerical score representing the outcome of a review process for a decision, typically in the context of loan applications, credit scoring, or other financial decision-making processes. This score quantifies the likelihood of a positive outcome based on the review, where higher scores indicate a greater probability of approval.

This field represents the high score of the outcome risk level, quantifying the potential risk associated with a particular outcome. It is calculated based on various risk factors and indicators, providing a numerical representation of the highest level of risk identified. The score is a floating-point number where higher values indicate greater risk.
Indicates whether a transaction was fraudulent. TRUE means the transaction was identified as fraud, FALSE means it was not.

A numerical score representing the medium-level risk associated with a specific outcome. This score is calculated based on various risk factors and metrics, providing an assessment of the potential medium-level risk. It is used to gauge the likelihood of an outcome falling within a medium risk category.

This field represents the quantified score of the lowest risk level associated with a specific outcome. It is a floating-point number that quantifies the minimal risk, with higher values indicating lower risk levels. This score is used in risk assessment models to evaluate and categorize the potential risk associated with different outcomes.

Represents the score calculated to determine the necessity of Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) under the PSD2 regulation. A lower score indicates a lower likelihood of requiring SCA, based on the transaction's risk assessment.
A numerical score representing the likelihood of a transaction being fraudulent. The score ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, where a higher score indicates a higher probability of fraud.
This field represents the original amount of the transaction credited to the receiver's account, before any fees or adjustments. It is expressed in the transaction's original currency.
A unique identifier for a payment transaction, typically used for tracking and reconciliation purposes.

A descriptive reason provided for the status of an external entity, process, or transaction. This field captures specific reasons that are external to the system, indicating why an item is in its current state.
The city in which the receiver's bank is located. This field is used to identify the geographical location of the bank for transaction processing and compliance purposes.

This field represents the initial decision made by an external entity or system, typically in the context of a financial application or transaction approval process. It indicates whether the application or transaction was preliminarily approved or not based on the external entity's criteria.
The currency in which the transaction was originally processed for the receiver. This field indicates the type of currency used without any conversion.
Specifies the method through which notifications about change events are delivered to the subscriber.

related_business_terms.ChangeEvent: Any update or modification to the data or system that subscribers need to be informed about.
related_business_terms.Subscriber: An entity or individual who has opted to receive notifications about change events.

description: The code representing the currency in which billing transactions are denominated. This code follows the ISO 4217 currency code standard.
Indicates whether the record is used for scoring purposes. A TRUE value means the record is included in scoring calculations, while a FALSE value means it is not.

The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP) used by the device at the time of the event or transaction. This field captures the ISP information to help in analyzing the network provider's impact on user behavior, connectivity quality, and geographical user distribution.
Specifies the frequency at which a payment is set to recur. This field indicates the periodicity of the payment obligation.
The total amount of money that the receiver gets in a transaction, specified in the transaction's currency. This value does not account for any transaction fees or adjustments that may apply.
This column represents the total amount of money that the sender has transferred in a single transaction. It is recorded in the platform's default currency and includes decimals for precise amounts.
Indicates whether Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) is required for a transaction. SCA is a requirement aimed at increasing the security of electronic payments.

Represents the current balance in the sender's account in a financial transaction. The balance is expressed in the account's currency and reflects the available funds after the transaction is initiated but before it is completed.

Represents the total balance in a financial institution's overnight account at the end of the banking day. This balance reflects the amount available in the account that can be used for overnight investments or to meet reserve requirements.

The date when the sender's account was originally opened, represented as the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970). This field is used to assess the age of the account for risk and trust evaluations.
Specifies the strategy used for the treatment or intervention in a financial outcome analysis, detailing the method or approach taken to achieve financial goals or rectify issues.

This column contains data related to VocaLink, a payment systems company which provides services for banks, corporates, and government departments. The data typically includes transactional information, payment processing details, and other relevant financial data processed by VocaLink.

This field represents the effectiveness score of a 1-way SMS strategy as part of a treatment or intervention outcome. The score is calculated based on various metrics such as engagement rate, response rate, and desired action completion rate, providing an indication of how well the strategy performed in achieving its objectives.
The UNIX timestamp representing the exact date and time when an event was created in the system. This value is measured in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 GMT).

This score represents the effectiveness of a treatment strategy, specifically measured through SMS (Short Message Service) communication, in achieving desired outcomes. It quantifies the impact of SMS-based interventions on treatment adherence or patient engagement, with higher scores indicating greater effectiveness.

Indicates the level of financial vulnerability of a customer, as assessed by specific criteria or algorithms. This marker helps in identifying customers who might need additional support or tailored services.

A numerical score representing the effectiveness of mobile push notification strategies in achieving desired outcomes. The score is calculated based on various factors such as user engagement, conversion rates, and overall performance of the push notification campaign. A higher score indicates a more effective strategy.
A code representing the gender of the customer. This field uses specific codes to indicate the customer's gender, ensuring privacy and standardization across datasets.
The date and time when a customer registered, represented as a UNIX timestamp (the number of seconds since the UNIX Epoch, January 1, 1970).

A numerical score representing the predicted outcome or effectiveness of having no treatment strategy applied. This score is used in the context of evaluating different treatment strategies to determine the baseline effectiveness of no intervention.

This field represents the citizenship of the customer, indicating the country in which the customer holds citizenship. It is important for understanding the customer's legal and regulatory obligations, as well as for reporting and compliance purposes.

A Unix timestamp representing the last time the Financial Information Verification (FIV) marker for a customer was updated. This field is used to track changes in the verification status of a customer's financial information.

The Unix timestamp representing the date and time at which the customer's earnings amount was last captured or updated in the system. This field is used to track the temporal aspect of the earnings data, ensuring that financial calculations and reporting can be accurately performed based on the most recent data available.
Indicates the status of a customer's enrollment in phone banking services, specifying whether the service is currently active, inactive, or in a state that requires further action or verification.

This field represents the current balance in a customer's account. It reflects the total amount of money available in the account at the current moment, accounting for all deposits, withdrawals, and other transactions up to the present time.
The first name of the customer as recorded in account details or transaction records.

This field represents the total amount of money debited from a current account in a single month. It includes all transactions that reduce the account balance, such as withdrawals, payments, and transfers out. The value is recorded in the account's currency.
This field represents the monthly salary amount of a customer in USD. It captures the gross monthly income before any deductions like taxes or retirement contributions.
The last name of a customer as recorded in their official account or profile information. This field is used for identification, personalization, and communication purposes.
The city where the customer's primary residence is located. This information is collected for demographic analysis and personalized marketing.
The street address of the customer's home, including house number, street name, and any applicable unit number. This address is used for billing and shipping purposes.

This field represents the ZIP code of the customer's home address. It is used to identify the geographical location and postal address for the customer. This information can be utilized for shipping, billing, and regional analysis purposes.
This field represents the geographical region where the customer's primary residence is located. It is identified by standard region abbreviations or codes.
Represents the ZIP or area code associated with a customer's home address. This code helps in identifying the geographical location or region of the customer's residence.
A two-letter code representing the country of residence of the customer, following the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.
The Unix timestamp representing the last time the customer's home address was updated in the system. This field captures the time in seconds since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).
The street address used for correspondence with the customer. This address may differ from the customer's primary or residential address and is often used for mailing purposes.
This field represents the geographical region associated with the customer's correspondence address. It is used to identify the location for mailing and communication purposes.
This field represents the ZIP code of the address where customers prefer to receive correspondence. It is used for mailing purposes and to ensure accurate delivery of physical documents or products.

This field represents the ZIP or area code extracted from the mailing address provided by the customer for correspondence purposes. It is used to identify the geographical location of the customer's mailing address.
The city part of the address to which all correspondence for the customer should be sent. This field captures the city name for mailing purposes and may differ from the customer's residential city.

This field represents the ISO country codes corresponding to the countries of the customers' mailing addresses. It is used to identify the country part of the address for international correspondence.

The primary contact phone number for a customer's home. It is used for communication purposes, including service notifications, billing inquiries, and customer support. The format includes country code and does not contain any separators.

This field contains the mobile phone number of the customer, including the country code but excluding any formatting characters such as dashes or spaces. It is used as a primary contact method for customer communication and verification purposes.

The Unix timestamp representing the last time the customer's correspondence address was updated in the system. This integer value counts the number of seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1 1970 00:00:00 GMT).
