The Unix timestamp indicating the last time the customer's email address was updated in the system. This value is represented as the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z).
The Unix timestamp indicating the last time the customer's home phone number was updated in the system. This field represents the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970).

This field stores the daytime work phone number of a customer, including the country code without any separators. It is primarily used for contacting the customer regarding work-related matters during standard business hours.

A Unix timestamp representing the last time the customer's work phone number was updated in the system. This integer value counts the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).

A Unix timestamp representing the last time a customer's mobile phone number was updated in the system. The value is stored as an integer, indicating the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).

The Unix timestamp representing the last time the customer's business phone number was updated in the system. This field captures the exact date and time the update occurred, measured in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).

A unique identifier assigned to each record in the financial data zone, ensuring data integrity and facilitating data management and retrieval. This identifier is immutable and follows a specific format to maintain consistency across the database.

This field represents the business phone number associated with a customer's account. It is used for business communication purposes. The phone number is stored in a standard numeric format without any special characters or spaces.

The timestamp indicating when a record was inserted into the BigQuery table. This field is automatically populated by the system and is used to track the exact time and date when data was added to the database. It is crucial for auditing, data synchronization, and understanding data freshness.

This field contains JSON-formatted strings representing the outcome of a particular process, such as a transaction approval process. Each string is a JSON object with keys and values providing details on the result.

Indicates whether the data row represents historical data. Historical data refers to information that records past events and transactions. A value of TRUE means the row contains historical data, while FALSE indicates the data is current or real-time.
Indicates whether an action is required or not. TRUE means an action is required, while FALSE means no action is necessary.

This column contains JSON-formatted data representing the outcomes of financial assessments, including risk levels and decision outcomes. Each entry is a structured object with keys for 'risk', indicating the risk level assessed, and 'decision', indicating the final decision made based on the assessment.

Indicates the level of financial vulnerability of a customer based on internal assessments or interactions. This classification helps in tailoring financial advice, products, and services to better suit the customer's needs.

A unique identifier representing different safety indicators used to classify and evaluate the safety performance or status of various entities or operations. Each code corresponds to a specific safety-related condition or measure.

A unique identifier used to mark customers associated with private banking services. This marker indicates the customer's enrollment in specialized banking services tailored for individuals with high net worth, offering personalized financial and banking advice.

Categorizes customers based on the value they bring to the company, their investment size, or their relationship duration. This segmentation helps in tailoring financial products, services, and communication strategies to fit the specific needs of each segment.

A unique identifier assigned to each customer interaction or feedback captured through voice channels. This ID is used to track and manage customer feedback, inquiries, or issues reported via voice communication platforms.

The Unix timestamp representing the date and time when the Customer Voice ID was last updated. This value is recorded as an integer, reflecting the number of seconds that have elapsed since the Unix epoch (00:00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970).
The precise point in time when an event or transaction was concluded, recorded in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
The exact date and time when an event or transaction begins, recorded in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

The date and time when the record was last updated, represented in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This timestamp includes the year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and millisecond, providing precise tracking of when data modifications occur.
The timestamp indicating when the record was inserted into the BigQuery table. This field is automatically populated by the system and is used to track the exact time data was added to the database.

A unique identifier representing the specific lifecycle stage of a financial product, customer, or transaction.
